root_cause.text: The `drm_gem_change_handle_ioctl()` function lacked validation to ensure the userspace-provided GEM handle did not exceed `INT_MAX`, causing `idr_alloc()` to interpret the unsigned 32-bit value as a negative signed integer and trigger a kernel warning.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds an explicit check `if (args->new_handle > INT_MAX) return -EINVAL;` before passing the handle to `idr_alloc()`, directly addressing the CVE description which states that passing a new handle larger than `INT_MAX` triggers `WARN_ON_ONCE(start < 0)` inside `idr_alloc()`.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement calls idr_alloc() with args->new_handle without validating that it doesn't exceed INT_MAX. When userspace provides a handle value greater than INT_MAX, the unsigned 32-bit value gets interpreted as a negative signed integer by idr_alloc(), triggering a kernel warning. The fix added an explicit bounds check (if (args->new_handle > INT_MAX)) before this call to prevent the sign-extension error.
